title: Slack for marketers on Mac: campaign channels, approvals and shortcuts, with Lazur in 2026

description: Slack for marketers on Mac: set up campaign channels, threads and approvals, learn the shortcuts that matter, and ask Lazur for help by voice.

intro: Slack for marketers on Mac works best when each campaign has its own channel, feedback lives in threads, and approvals run on emoji reactions. Learn the Command shortcuts for search and unread messages first, since you use them every day. This page covers setup, shortcuts, prices and common mistakes, then shows where Lazur fits.
tldr: Give each campaign its own channel with a description, and star the few channels you open every day.
Keep feedback in threads, and track approvals with a reaction key that the whole team agrees on before the review starts.
Learn ⌘G, ⌘F, ⌘K, ⌘J and ⌘, first. Slack does not allow custom keyboard shortcuts.
Pro costs $7.25 per user per month billed annually. Check the pricing page before you plan around marketing templates.
Hold ⌥⌘ to ask Lazur where things are on screen. Lazur draws a circle around them, and you click them yourself.

blocks.text: What a marketer's Slack looks like on a Mac

Most marketing teams use Slack for three jobs. They run campaigns, they review work, and they ask each other for things. Each job needs its own habit. Campaigns need channels people can find. Reviews need threads. Requests need one place where nothing gets buried.

On a Mac, Slack runs as its own app with a sidebar on the left. The sidebar lists channels, direct messages and apps. The message list sits in the middle, and the search bar sits at the top. Most of your day happens in those three areas.

The Mac app updates often. The latest stable build in Slack's release notes is 4.53.283, dated November 9, 2026. That release was a bug-fix update. The three most recent release notes mention no changes to menus, the sidebar or search. Check the release notes if a menu item moves on you.
Set up one channel per campaign

Create one channel for each campaign, launch or sub-team. Slack's marketing guide recommends this pattern, with a description on every channel. Start each name with the team or project. Add a quarter or year only when the work ends on a date.

To make a new channel, follow [how to create a channel in Slack on Mac](/how-to/create-a-channel-in-slack). Choose a public channel when the whole team should see the work. Choose a private channel for sensitive work, such as unannounced launches or pricing tests.
Use these naming rules. They hold up over a year.

items: Name channels after the work, such as paid-social, spring-launch or press-kit.
Put the owner in the description, not in the name.
Keep names short enough to read in the sidebar at a glance.
Archive a channel the day its campaign closes.

blocks.text: Descriptions do more than names. A new freelancer should read the description and know the goal, the owner and where the final files live.
Star, group and mute to keep the sidebar readable

Star the channels you open every day. Starred channels stay at the top, so you stop scrolling. Slack's marketing guide also suggests custom sidebar sections. Use them to group channels by client or by quarter.

Mute the channels you read once a week. Muting keeps them out of your way without leaving them. The how-to covers the exact steps: [how to mute a channel in Slack on Mac](/how-to/mute-a-channel-in-slack).
Common mistake: starring every channel. A star list with every channel in it is just a longer sidebar.
Use threads so feedback stays in one place

A thread keeps each reply attached to the message it answers. Slack's marketing guide recommends threads for focused feedback. Use them for every review. A designer can answer the banner comment without burying the headline discussion.

To reply in a thread, hover over the message and choose the reply option. Shortcuts and fixes are in [how to reply in a thread in Slack on Mac](/how-to/reply-in-a-thread-in-slack). Find every thread you follow in the Threads view, described in [how to view threads in Slack on Mac](/how-to/open-the-threads-view-in-slack).

Worked example. A copywriter posts a few headlines in #campaign-spring-launch. You ask reviewers to reply in one thread under that post, with the headline they pick. You end with one list of votes, not a scatter of messages across the channel.
Track approvals with emoji reactions

Emoji reactions are the cheapest approval system you can run. Agree on the reactions before the review starts. A check mark can mean approved. An eyes emoji can mean reviewing. An x can mean changes needed. Write the key in the channel description.

Slack's marketing guide describes emoji reactions as a way to track approvals. Pin the key so it stays visible. The steps are in [how to pin a message in Slack on Mac](/how-to/pin-a-message-in-slack).

Reactions have one weak spot. People forget to react. Post a short status message each week in the same channel. Set a reminder for yourself with [how to set a reminder in Slack on Mac](/how-to/set-a-reminder-in-slack).
Workflow Builder for intake forms and weekly status

Workflow Builder turns repeat tasks into small automated flows. Slack's marketing article gives four examples. They are intake forms, welcome messages, weekly status update reminders, and emoji-triggered FAQ links.

An intake form works best for requests. Ask for the goal, the deadline, the audience and the channel. The form posts into one request channel. Your team stops asking for those details in direct messages.
Start with these four flows.

items: An intake form that posts new requests to a #help request channel.
A weekly status reminder for each campaign channel.
A welcome message for anyone who joins a campaign channel.
An emoji trigger that posts the brand FAQ link.

blocks.text: Slack's marketing article says marketing templates, such as pre-formatted canvases, lists and workflows, need a paid plan. Check your plan before you build a process around a template. Give every workflow one owner, named in its description, so a broken flow gets fixed.
Slack prices and plans for marketing teams

Slack's pricing page lists per-user prices. Pro costs $7.25 per user per month billed annually, or $8.75 billed monthly. Business+ costs $15 per user per month billed annually. Enterprise+ costs $45 per user per month billed annually. Prices can change, so check the page before you buy.

blocks.text: The free plan has real limits. Messages stay saved and searchable for 90 days. Free workspaces get up to 10 apps. The pricing page states no file storage limit.

Some third-party sources say older messages get hidden or deleted. Slack's pricing page only says messages are saved and searchable for 90 days. Treat that as the promise you can rely on. Move decisions out of Slack before the window closes.
Slack Mac shortcuts for marketers
Slack's keyboard shortcuts page lists the Mac commands that cover most of a marketer's day. Learn them in this order, because you will use the first two every hour.

items: ⌘G starts a search across the workspace. Guide: [how to search messages in Slack on Mac](/how-to/search-messages-in-slack).
⌘F searches only the open conversation. It is good for finding a link in a long channel. See [how to search in a conversation in Slack on Mac](/how-to/search-inside-a-conversation-in-slack).
⌘K jumps to a conversation by name. See [how to jump to a conversation in Slack on Mac](/how-to/jump-to-a-conversation-in-slack).
⌘J jumps to your first unread message.
⌘, opens preferences.
Esc or Shift+Esc marks messages as read in the current conversation.

blocks.text: One caveat applies. Slack's screen-reader help page lists ⌘K, but the main shortcuts page does not. Test ⌘K on your own build before you rely on it.
Custom shortcuts are not possible. Slack's shortcuts page says so directly. Build your habits around the defaults, starting with ⌘G.
For the full list on your build, read [how to show keyboard shortcuts in Slack on Mac](/how-to/show-the-keyboard-shortcuts-list-in-slack).
Jump to unread messages without losing mentions
Marketers come back from a meeting with a dozen channels changed. Start with ⌘J. It lands on the first unread message. Then work down one channel at a time, instead of opening everything at once.

Mark a message as unread when you need to return to it. The how-to covers the three dots menu and the Option-click method: [how to mark a message as unread in Slack on Mac](/how-to/mark-a-message-as-unread-in-slack).

Clearing every unread can hide a message from your manager. Read mentions and direct messages first. Then clear the channels you do not need. When you are sure, use [how to mark all messages as read in Slack on Mac](/how-to/mark-all-messages-as-read-in-slack).
Notifications: keep the mentions and lose the noise

Notifications decide how much of your day Slack takes. Mute the noisy channels first. Then set a pause for focus time. The pause option sits in the profile menu, and the steps are in [how to pause notifications in Slack on Mac](/how-to/pause-notifications-in-slack).
Slack's screen-reader help page lists ⌘⌥S for a notifications summary. Use it when you come back from a long meeting. It shows what happened while you were away.

If alerts never appear, check macOS too. Open System Settings > Notifications > Slack and confirm that alerts are allowed. For the full set of fixes, read [how to fix Slack notifications not working on Mac](/how-to/fix-missing-notifications-in-slack).
Common mistake: turning on alerts for every channel. Keep alerts for mentions, direct messages and your campaign owners. Leave the rest in the sidebar.
Huddles, clips and canvases for campaign briefs

Slack's marketing guide lists three tools beyond chat. Huddles handle quick brainstorms and screen-share reviews. Clips send a short video or audio update that people watch when they have time. Canvases hold a shared brief or a task checklist.
Use one canvas per campaign. Put the goal, the audience, the deadline and the owner at the top. Pin the canvas in the channel so people find it fast.

Use a huddle when a review needs talking. Share your screen to walk through a deck or a live page. The steps are in [how to share screen in a Slack huddle on Mac](/how-to/share-your-screen-in-a-huddle-in-slack).
Use a clip when a meeting would waste everyone's time. A short walkthrough of a dashboard works well. People can watch it on their own schedule.
Work with agencies and freelancers in Slack Connect

Slack's marketing guide recommends Slack Connect for agencies and freelancers. Slack Connect lets people outside your company join a shared channel. That channel becomes the shared space for the project.

Set the rules before the first invite. Agree who owns the channel, who approves files, and where final versions live. Write those rules in the channel description, so the agency reads them on day one.
Common mistake: using the agency channel for internal talk. Keep your own debate in an internal channel. Invite the agency only to the work they need.
Where Lazur fits in Slack on a Mac

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. It lives in the notch and works in any app, Slack included. It is not a plugin or add-in for Slack. It helps you find things and get steps right. It does not click for you.
Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud. Ask where the approvals thread is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. You click it yourself.
Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click before it names the next one. This helps with menus you use once a quarter.

Hold fn to dictate. Dictation writes clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. It works for status updates, long replies and brief notes. Snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots are there too.

Lazur also covers everyday tasks by voice. It handles timers, Apple Reminders, Calendar events, notes, music and volume, opening apps and links, web search and Shortcuts. Ask for a reminder to check approvals, and it lands in Apple Reminders.
Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It returns a summary and a report. Use it for competitor pricing pages, then check the source yourself.

Privacy matters with work chat. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models. Lazur keeps a memory of what you asked and did, on your Mac.
A launch week in Slack, step by step
Here is one launch week, from start to finish. Each day uses a habit from this page.

items: Monday: the brief lives in a canvas, and the weekly status reminder posts to the campaign channel.
Tuesday: a few headline drafts go into one thread, and reviewers react with their pick.
Wednesday: the agency joins through Slack Connect and finds the brief link in the channel description.
Thursday: ⌘G finds the final asset link, and you pin it to the channel.
Friday: ⌘J takes you to unread messages, one channel at a time, and you mark the rest read.

blocks.text: The week runs on channels, threads and reactions. Lazur helps when you forget a shortcut or a menu. It does not replace the habits.
How much time Slack can save, and how to test it

Forrester's study, commissioned by Slack, models 100 minutes saved per marketer per week by Year 3. The model uses a composite organization. It draws on six interviews and a survey of 558 marketing professionals. Read it as a vendor estimate, not a result for your team.
The same study reports a 298% return on investment and payback in under 6 months. Those figures depend on its assumptions. Check them against your own costs.

Atlassian's State of Teams 2025 found that teams waste 25% of their time searching for answers. That figure covers knowledge workers in general, not marketers alone. It still shows why search habits matter.

Test it yourself. Track your searches for one week. Write down what you wanted, how long it took, and whether you found it. Repeat after a month with the channels and shortcuts from this page. Compare the two logs.
Mistakes marketers make in Slack on Mac

items: One channel for each person. Channels should follow the work, not the people.
Feedback in direct messages. Nobody else sees it, and it gets lost.
Blank channel descriptions. New members cannot tell what the channel is for.
Relying on the free plan for long-term history. Messages stay searchable for 90 days, according to Slack's pricing page.
Searching the whole workspace for answers that are pinned or in a canvas. Look there first.
Skipping the Mac release notes. A menu change can cost you time you did not plan for.

blocks.text: Fix one mistake each week. The small fixes add up, and each one makes the next search shorter.
A one-week setup plan for your Mac

items: Day one: create a channel for each active campaign and write a description for each.
Day two: star the channels you open daily and mute the ones you read rarely.
Day three: build one Workflow Builder intake form for new requests.
Day four: agree on the approval reactions and pin the key in each review channel.
Day five: learn ⌘G, ⌘K, ⌘J and ⌘, and test ⌘K on your build.

blocks.text: Then start the search log from the last section. The log shows which habits work. Use it to decide what to change next week.
What to do next

Download Lazur from [the download page](/download). It runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. Lazur has a free trial, and [the pricing page](/pricing) lists the plans.

faq.question: Is there a Slack app for Mac that marketers can use?
faq.answer: Yes. Slack has a desktop app for Mac. The latest stable build in Slack's release notes is 4.53.283, dated November 9, 2026. Marketers use the same app as everyone else, with channels, threads and Workflow Builder.

faq.question: Which Slack plan do marketing teams need?
faq.answer: Slack's marketing article says marketing templates need a paid plan. Pro costs $7.25 per user per month billed annually. Check the pricing page for what Business+ and Enterprise+ include before you decide.

faq.question: Can I change Slack's keyboard shortcuts on Mac?
faq.answer: No. Slack's keyboard shortcuts page says it is not currently possible to set custom keyboard shortcuts for Slack. Learn the default keys, and use the how-to page for the full list.

faq.question: What happens to Slack messages on the free plan after 90 days?
faq.answer: Slack's pricing page says free-plan messages are saved and searchable for 90 days. It does not say what happens after that. Some third-party sources disagree, so save important decisions outside Slack.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Slack?
faq.answer: Lazur works in any app on your Mac, Slack included. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about the screen. Lazur answers out loud and points at things. It does not click buttons for you, and it is not a Slack plugin or add-in.

faq.question: Does Lazur send my Slack messages to AI providers?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

faq.question: Why does a Slack shortcut do nothing on my Mac?
faq.answer: Click the Slack window so it has focus, then try the key again. If it still fails, test it on your build. Slack's help pages disagree on ⌘K, so check that key first.

faq.question: Can agencies and freelancers work in my Slack without seeing everything?
faq.answer: Slack's marketing guide recommends Slack Connect for agencies and freelancers. Use a shared channel for the project only. Put the rules in the channel description before you send the first invite.
